info.name: Transactions System
info.description:
Full end-to-end test flow for the multi-tenant transaction platform.

Two distinct API key types:
- **Source key** — held by external providers (OMT, Wish). Can POST transactions on behalf of any company via `/ingest/:sourceCode/transactions`, and discover companies via `GET /ingest/companies`.
- **Company key** — held by the company itself. **It is NOT read-only**: it authenticates as the company's owner, so besides reading (transactions, wallets, ledger, analytics, exports) it can request and cancel withdrawals, payouts and loads and create Whish payment links (folder 05b does exactly that). Keys have no scopes — treat one like a password that can move money. It cannot ingest (only a source key can), and it cannot manage API keys, the team or the CRM webhook (dashboard session only).

Run the requests **in order** from the top folder down:

1. **00 — Health** — sanity check the API is up
2. **01 — Admin** — log in as super admin, create a test company
3. **02 — Company Owner** — log in as the new owner, create a company key
4. **02b — Admin: Source Keys** — mint a source key for a provider (e.g. OMT)
5. **03 — Ingestion (external provider)** — discover companies, then POST a transaction using the source key + companySlug
6. **04 — Owner reads** — wallets, transactions, ledger
7. **05 — Withdrawals** — request one, then admin approves with a reference
8. **07 — Analytics** — admin dashboards
9. **08 — Negative tests** — confirm validation/auth errors fire correctly
10. **09 — Network fee (super admin)** — switch on a 1% deposit network fee for the test company, ingest a deposit, read the fee back with the company key, then switch it off again (local/staging only)

The collection has **test scripts that auto-capture** the CSRF token, company ID, owner credentials, source/company API keys, and withdrawal ID into collection variables — so you just click Send in order and everything flows.

**Cookies**: Postman manages them per-host. When you switch from admin to owner login, the older session is overwritten automatically. If you want to log out fully, click the Cookies icon and clear `localhost`.

item.name: 03 — Ingestion (external provider)
item.description:
Run **02b — Admin: Source Keys** first to mint `{{sourceApiKey}}`. These requests use only the Bearer API key — no cookies, no CSRF. This simulates the real external integration where OMT / Wish / banks POST to the platform.

Key identifies the **source**. The body's `companyId` identifies which company the transaction is **for**.

exec: const j = pm.response.json().data; // responses are enveloped: { success, statusCode, data }
pm.test('Returns an array of companies', () => pm.expect(j.data).to.be.an('array'));

request.description: External provider startup: discover the list of ACTIVE companies, cache their slugs. Returns `{ data: [{ slug, name, defaultCurrency }, ...] }`. Only callable with a source key. (Undocumented for partners — sources are normally handed their slugs directly.)

exec: const j = pm.response.json().data; // responses are enveloped: { success, statusCode, data }
pm.test('Fee is hidden from sources (no commissionAmount)', () => pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property('commissionAmount'));
pm.test('Net is hidden from sources (no netAmount)', () => pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property('netAmount'));
pm.test('Network fee is hidden from sources (no networkFeeAmount)', () => pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property('networkFeeAmount'));

request.description:
Matches the **1–100 USD FIXED 1** seeded commission rule. The `{{$timestamp}}` keeps the externalTransactionId unique on re-run.

**Payload fields** (the API recognises these plain-string fields; any extra keys are preserved):
- `customer` — the *sender* / payer name
- `tradingAccount` — the *recipient* / beneficiary account
- `phone` — a contact phone number
- `note` — free-text comment from the provider
- any other keys under `payload` are preserved as-is
**101–300 USD FIXED 5** bracket.
**301–1000 PERCENTAGE 2%** → fee 10, net 490.
**Send this twice.** The second response should return the **same `id`** as the first — proving the dedup works. No duplicate row is created.
Returns the transaction plus all ledger entries (typically 3: DEBIT EXTERNAL, CREDIT AVAILABLE, CREDIT FEE).

exec: const j = pm.response.json().data; // responses are enveloped: { success, statusCode, data }
pm.test('networkFeeAmount is present ("0" when not charged)', () => pm.expect(j).to.have.property('networkFeeAmount'));
pm.test('totalAmount == netAmount + feeAmount + networkFeeAmount', () => pm.expect(cents(j.totalAmount)).to.equal(cents(j.netAmount) + cents(j.feeAmount) + cents(j.networkFeeAmount)));

item.name: 08 — Negative tests
item.description: Confirm the platform rejects bad input safely.

request.description: Uses the company-owned key `{{apiKey}}` to try to ingest. Must return 403 — only source keys can ingest.
Run as company owner. Should return 409 `CONFLICT: Wallet balance would become negative`.
Run as admin. Must fail validation: the platform forces operators to record proof of payment before flipping the ledger.
Run as company owner. Send WITHOUT the `x-csrf-token` header — the CSRF guard should return 403.

item.name: 09 — Network fee (super admin)
item.description:
Exercises the optional per-company **network fee** — a second platform fee charged next to the commission, configured by a `SUPER_ADMIN` per company and per flow (`TRANSACTION` = deposits, `WITHDRAWAL`, `PAYOUT`, `LOAD`) as a `PERCENTAGE` or a `FIXED` amount. It is **not** a blockchain/gas fee and is unrelated to `payoutDetails.network` on CRYPTO payouts. Companies cannot set it; they only read `networkFeeAmount` (`"0"` when not charged).

Flow: read the config → switch on 1% for deposits → ingest a 100 USD deposit with the **source** key (the response must carry no fee fields) → read it back with the **company** key (`networkFeeAmount` = `"1"`) → switch the fee off again → confirm `enabled: true` with no rates is rejected.

Needs `{{companyId}}`, `{{companySlug}}`, `{{sourceApiKey}}` and `{{apiKey}}` from folders 01–03. The admin routes need a dashboard session + CSRF (never an API key), and `PUT` is `SUPER_ADMIN`-only.

**Local / staging only.** These requests change what a company is charged — never point this folder at production.

item.name: (switch to admin) Login as super admin

request.description: The network-fee routes are admin routes: they take a dashboard session (cookie + CSRF), never an API key.

exec: const j = pm.response.json().data; // responses are enveloped: { success, statusCode, data }
pm.test('Shape is { enabled, rates[] }', () => { pm.expect(j.enabled).to.be.a('boolean'); pm.expect(j.rates).to.be.an('array'); });
console.log('Network fee before this folder:', JSON.stringify(j));

request.description: Returns `{ enabled, rates: [{ operationType, feeType, feeValue }] }` — rates in flow order (deposits, withdrawals, payouts, loads); a flow that is absent is not charged. Ships OFF: a new company reads `{ "enabled": false, "rates": [] }`. Readable by `SUPER_ADMIN` and `ADMIN_OPERATOR`.

item.name: Enable a 1% network fee on deposits

exec: pm.test('Only deposits are charged, 1%', () => pm.expect(j.rates).to.eql([{ operationType: 'TRANSACTION', feeType: 'PERCENTAGE', feeValue: '1' }]));

request.description: `SUPER_ADMIN` only (an `ADMIN_OPERATOR` gets `403`). Replaces the **whole** configuration: the master switch plus every flow's rate — a flow left out is not charged. Every value must be greater than 0: a `PERCENTAGE` is a rate (at most 100, up to 8 decimals); a `FIXED` value is dollars (at most 2 decimals). The change applies to the next operation; existing rows keep the fees frozen on them.

item.name: Ingest 100 USD with the source key (no fee fields)

exec: pm.test('Source never sees the network fee', () => pm.expect(j).to.not.have.property('networkFeeAmount'));

request.description: The network fee is computed alongside the commission, inside the same booking — and is just as invisible to the source: the ingest response is unchanged. Saves the id as `{{networkFeeTransactionId}}`.

exec: pm.test('DEDUCTED deposit: amount == commissionAmount + networkFeeAmount + netAmount', () => pm.expect(cents(j.amount)).to.equal(cents(j.commissionAmount) + cents(j.networkFeeAmount) + cents(j.netAmount)));
console.log('commission', j.commissionAmount, '· network fee', j.networkFeeAmount, '· net', j.netAmount);

request.description: The company sees both fees. With the seeded global rule (0–100 USD → FIXED 1) this reads `commissionAmount` `"1"`, `networkFeeAmount` `"1"`, `netAmount` `"98"`. Try `/detail` on the same id to see the fourth ledger leg: `NETWORK_FEE` CREDIT `1`.

item.name: Restore: switch the network fee off

request.description: Puts the test company back to "not charged". Switching off may also keep the rates (send them with `enabled: false`) so turning it back on does not lose the setup; here they are cleared. The deposit booked above keeps its frozen fee.

item.name: Enabled with no rates is rejected (400)

request.description: Turning the switch on requires a rate for at least one flow ("Set a network fee for at least one flow, or turn the network fee off").
